messages:
lee_ops: Heads-up: our production consumer hit repeated `Invalid JSON` errors when parsing the API stream for json_mode. Error sample: "Unexpected end of input at char 142".

jenny_support: Sorry about that. Can you paste the raw bytes or a screenshot of the first few chunks? Also confirm whether you assume one object per streaming chunk.

lee_ops: We do assume near-atomic items in each chunk (previously that was true). Repro call: `curl -sS https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-beta-2","json_mode":true,"stream":true,"max_tokens":1200}'`

lee_ops: Raw chunk dump (copied as-is):
``
chunk A: [{"uid":"u1","content":"a"},{"uid":"u2","content":"b"},{"uid":"u3","content":"c",
chunk B: "meta":{"src":"agent"}},{"uid":"u4","content":"d"}]
```

tom_sre: This looks like a mid-object split + an extra nested `meta` node that wasn't in the usual schema. If a client tries to parse per chunk it fails.

runtime_dev: I'm replaying the request id (rid_0xabc901) in staging. I can repro chunk boundary inside an object when the server flushes due to buffer pressure. Recorded boundary: `...,"content":"c",
"meta":{"src":"agent"} ...` which yields invalid JSON if parsed early.

jenny_support: Quick workarounds: 1) set `stream:false` to get a single validated array response; 2) implement an incremental buffer on client and only attempt JSON parse when brackets match; 3) switch to NDJSON (one JSON object per line) if your consumer can adapt.

lee_ops: Switching to `stream:false` fixes it but increases P95 latency. NDJSON would be workable for our pipeline. Any chance you can offer a server-side compatibility option?

ingrid_eng: We can add a short-term server heuristic to prefer flushing at top-level item boundaries when `json_mode:true` and streaming is enabled. I'll open an internal task. Long term, we want a documented streaming contract.

runtime_dev: Filed INC-4667: "json_mode stream may split items; add chunk-safe option and tests". Added replay logs and the staging replay that reproduces the mid-object split.

repro_bot: INC-4667 created and assigned to eng-runtime. Repro steps attached.

lee_ops: Another wrinkle: some items have `meta` nested and some outputs use `val` instead of `content`. Our strict validator fails. Is model output variability expected?

ingrid_eng: Yes, two possible causes: model sampling noise (field aliasing) or an alternate fine-tuned variant that emits slightly different keys. We recently rolled a small variant to some traffic.

tom_sre: Short-term we recommend client-side normalization: map aliases (`val` -> `content`, `uid` -> `id`) and supply defaults for missing required fields. We'll share a small normalization snippet in the ticket.

jenny_support: We can also offer to pin your org to the stable variant we verified for strict schema adherence. That reduces variance but may alter latency/cost slightly. Would you like us to evaluate pinning?

lee_ops: Yes please pin if it stabilizes schema. We prefer stable keys over marginal perf wins.

finance_alert: Note: disabling streaming or repeated replays has increased this customer's token egress during debugging. If pinning leads to longer decodes we may see billing impact; finance will flag large surges.

runtime_dev: As a medium-term improvement we propose two product changes: (1) add `json_chunk_safe: true` (server will prefer flush boundaries at item edges when feasible), and (2) a `schema` request argument that instructs the model/runtime to strictly format keys (we'll log adherence rates). We'll prototype both.

lee_ops: That sounds great. For immediate timeline can you add a staging flag so we can validate in our environment before full rollout?

ingrid_eng: Yes, I'll enable a canary for your org in staging. We'll include a test harness so you can opt-in to verify NDJSON vs array behaviors.

jenny_support: Action items summarized: (A) customer will try NDJSON adapter or buffering while we work on server heuristics; (B) eng-runtime to implement flush-heuristic change and add INC-4667 updates; (C) eng to evaluate pinning the stable variant for this org; (D) finance to monitor token spikes.

lee_ops: Thanks team. I'll paste any new request ids if we see more failures. Appreciate the pin/canary offer.

tom_sre: Also adding a short runbook entry: "Parsing streamed json_mode safely" with sample code to accumulate chunks and only parse when top-level brackets are balanced, plus an NDJSON example. Link will be added to INC-4667.

jenny_support: Closing this thread for now; we will update INC-4667 and DM when the canary is ready. :handshake:

finance_alert: Finance watching token usage; will reach out if monthly delta exceeds threshold.

lee_ops: Good work, thanks all.
